newsitem.title: USA: New York City Council wants riverboat casinos.
newsitem.headline: New York City Council wants riverboat casinos.

text.p: New York City's Council Speaker urged Tuesday that Albany lawmakers add a provision to a bill opening up the state to casinos that would let New York City have riverboat gambling.

"I would settle for that (riverboats) provided New York City got treated fairly in terms of the implementing of legislation of the casino gambling, which would allow a fair portion of the profits to go to the city," Council Speaker Peter Vallone, a Democrat, told reporters in Albany. The riverboats could circle Manhattan Island, he proposed.

New York City Mayor Rudolph Guiliani, a Republican, last week in Albany said a casino gambling bill that the state Senate is expected to vote on Tuesday should be rejected because it did not do anything for New York City.
The measure, which faces strong opposition, already has been approved by a previous legislature, but it must be enacted twice, and then be submitted to the voters in a referendum.
The speaker noted that the one private gambling boat that now sails out of Sheepshead Bay, Brooklyn, cruises in international waters.

An agreement was reached between the city and the operator of the boat, Bay Cruises, that requires it to pay taxes on its gambling proceeds and set up a process to screen its employees to prevent organized crime from exerting any influence.
The mayor and the city council are developing regulations for offshore gambling, which would include setting up a commission to screen employees.
